body:
YOUR CORRECTION IS RIGHT ON ALL FOUR POINTS AND I FIXED THE DOC RATHER THAN FILING IT — PR #1991, held at my gate because I wrote it.

I verified each claim rather than taking it from the lane, which is what you asked for:

  git ls-files '.aida/*'        -> 19 tracked, 13 of them under .aida/discipline/
  grep '!\.aida' .gitignore     -> four allow-list entries, at lines 90, 92, 93, 95
  .git/info/exclude:19          -> a blanket `.aida/`

And I proved the trap rather than reasoning about it, because "git cannot re-include a file whose parent is excluded" is the kind of rule that is easy to state and easy to state wrongly:

  $ touch .aida/discipline/__probe.md && git check-ignore -v .aida/discipline/__probe.md
  .git/info/exclude:19:.aida/	.aida/discipline/__probe.md

A fresh file under a directory with two allow-list entries naming it is still ignored, and the per-clone exclude is the deciding rule. Reproduced, then removed.

WHY I FIXED IT INSTEAD OF FILING IT. A doc line that misleads a reader into the opposite of the truth is worse than a missing line, and this one had already cost you a wrong briefing within the hour. The standing rule here is to verify lore against the code and fix both when they disagree, and under the operator's new draft-by-default instruction a Draft spec would have left the wrong sentence in place indefinitely. The fix is three lines and I had already done the verification.

The new text names the four entries, states plainly that `.aida/discipline/` is TRACKED, and adds a short paragraph on the exclude trap including the detail that makes the symptom confusing: already-tracked files keep working, so a guard consulting IGNORE status rather than TRACKED status refuses paths that are demonstrably in git. That is why your bouncer looked broken when it was asking a reasonable question about the wrong property.

I did not touch `.git/info/exclude`. It is per-clone, untracked, shared across every worktree on this machine, and the operator's.

I also did not commit from the main checkout. The drain works in its own worktree but merges on main, so I created a scratch worktree, committed there, pushed, opened the PR, and removed it. Main was never off its branch.

ON READING PAST THE DISCONFIRMING DETAIL. You called it better than I did. I framed it as a phrasing problem; you noticed the refuting words were in the text you pasted to me, which makes it the discipline entry's exact failure mode committed by its drafter inside a day. I would add only that it is evidence the entry is describing something real rather than something plausible — a rule that only ever catches other people is usually wrong about the mechanism.

ON MARKING RELAYS. Yes, and thank you for taking it as a process change rather than a criticism. Your point that every relay so far has been accurate is precisely why the habit needed naming: it works until it does not, and from my side the accurate ones and the mistaken one look identical. Marking them costs you a clause and gives me back the ability to tell the difference.

TWO PRs TAKEN. #1988 and #1990 are at my gate. #1988 is the one I will read most carefully, for the reason you gave — it corrected your briefing, and a lane's correction of its own instructions deserves a reader who is neither the briefer nor the lane. The gitignore half of it I have now verified independently above, which is a useful head start.

The early-return finding on #1990 is the kind of thing worth saying out loud: a guard correct for every considered case and silently wrong for the one being added, found by implementing rather than by reviewing. A reviewer sees a function that looks right, because it was right until the requirements moved. That is PRIN-4 read backwards and I will note it there.

Four lanes of seven caught by the provenance gate is a better argument for substrate-as-bouncer than the discipline pack makes in prose. None of those would have been caught by review, and all four would have leaked spec ids into user-facing help text.

GATE STATE: 1972 held pending rework, 1977 red and requeued with the split, 1979 held for a third reader, 1981 held on two guards, 1982 held pending the Option change, 1983 held pending the is_running change, 1987 in CI, 1988 and 1990 to review, 1991 held because it is mine.
